payload.headline: Netflix slips below base fair value; growth slowing, chart weak; still waiting for 61

summary.thesis: Netflix is a grade-B cash machine priced near its base fair value, but slowing sales growth, falling estimates and a peak margin leave little margin of safety at 62.69.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for the 61.15–61.63 support zone or lower; swing: wait, no trade in a falling trend.

payload.happening: Netflix fell 2.87% to 62.69. That puts it below its 20-day (64.76), 50-day (69.6) and 200-day (80.6) averages, and all three are falling. There is no news since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-19, and analysts have cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3% over the last 30 days.
payload.business: The business itself is still strong. Sales over the last 12 months were 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 11.4B from 9.0B. Operating margin improved to 31.3% from 29.14%, and the share count fell 3.35% in a year, which means buybacks are adding to each share's value. Growth is slowing, though: quarterly sales growth was 11.85% versus 16.19% two quarters ago, and the filings flag that 'sales growth is slowing or stalled.' The main business risk is margin: 31% is the top of its 5-year range (17–31%), and the filings note that peaks like this usually fade. The balance sheet is not at risk: debt of 12.7B against 8.2B in cash means net debt of 4.4B, which is small next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. Today's drop comes with no news, so it changes sentiment and the chart, not the business. Segment data is not available, so we cannot tell where the slowdown is coming from.

worth.text: The stock trades at 17.8 times trailing earnings and 16.6 times next year's estimate. It sells for 5.2 times sales, against a peer median of 7.2, and sits at the 25th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. So it is cheap compared with its own history and with big-tech peers. A discounted cash flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 38.33 in the bear case, 65.31 in the base case and 78.29 in the bull case. The own-history price-to-sales method gives a wider 60.37–122.15. The gap between the methods comes down to one assumption: how fast cash flow grows. The current price implies starting free-cash-flow growth of 13.6%. That is close to recent sales growth (14.65% trailing, 14.95% over 3 years) but above the latest quarter's 11.85% and well above analysts' 5% next-year EPS growth. At 10% starting growth the value is 54.07; at 20% it is 80.74. Margin matters too: if operating margin fell to 23%, the value would be 60.29. (The valuation summary line in the data refers to a stale 64.54 price; the figures above use today's 62.69.)
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow keeps growing at about the 13.6% the price implies, even though quarterly sales growth has already slowed to 11.85% and margins sit at a 5-year peak.

bull: Free cash flow rose to 11.4B from 9.0B, and the share count fell 3.35%, so each share gets a bigger slice of the cash.
Price-to-sales of 5.2 is below the peer median of 7.2 and at the 25th percentile of its own 5-year range.
Operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%, which shows the business still gains profit as it grows.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
This quarter's EPS estimate was cut 7.3% in 30 days, and next year's 3.77 implies only 5% EPS growth.
Operating margin is at the top of its 17–31% five-year range; at 23% the DCF value falls to 60.29, and at 15% to 39.83.

levels.what: DCF base value; the stock is now just below it, so the margin of safety is thin
Bottom of the 61.15–61.63 support zone, the first area to start building a position
Low end of its own-history price-to-sales range, next to the 60 put strike with the most open interest (37561)

longterm.why: Quality is good (grade B) and the stock is cheap compared with its history and peers. But estimates are falling and the margin is at a peak, so the plan is to wait for the support zone, where there is more room for error.

swing.why: The stock is in a downtrend below all three falling averages, and the technical view is negative (lower highs and lower lows). Wait until it either holds 61.15–61.63 or closes back above the 20-day average of 64.76 and resistance at 64.84–65.32.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-19 come after the 2027-01-15 option expiry. Options price a move of about 11.7% by that expiry, and estimates are still being cut, so any entry ahead of the report should be small and made only at support.

change_mind: A close above 65.32, which would reclaim the 20-day average of 64.76 and break the first resistance zone, would ease the technical case against swing entries.
A break below 60.37, or another cut to the this-quarter EPS estimate of 0.68, would push the deeper value of 54.07 into focus.
If the 2027-01-19 report shows quarterly sales growth back toward 16.19% with operating margin holding near 31.3%, that would support the 80.74 high end.
payload.what_changed: The price fell from 64.54 to 62.69 with no news, slipping below the 65.31 base value but not reaching the 61.15 buy zone, so the view stays the same: wait.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
